title: finding(react/app-shell): an action's `params` bag is never template-evaluated and `action:button` does not inject the row — a metadata-authored `navigate_edit` cannot target the current record
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:ui` execution seat while implementing objectui#7440 (PR #7865) — recording, not claiming. Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

## The claim

**An action's `params` bag is never template-evaluated on any authoring channel, and `action:button` does not inject the surrounding row — so a metadata-authored `navigate_edit` button cannot be pointed at the record the user is looking at.** It can only carry a record id hard-coded at authoring time.

This is not "the handler is dead". `navigate_edit` is registered (`packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:487`), reachable from metadata, and works — objectui#7440's PR verifies all of that by rendering. What is missing is the one argument that makes it useful per row.

## Measured

`origin/main` `3faaa7d0f`, through the real production renderers, `SchemaRenderer` driving `action:button` inside a `RecordContextProvider` bound to `{ id: 'rec_1' }`, with `navigate_edit` registered the way `AppContent.tsx` registers it. Values read off the `ActionDef` the handler actually received:

```
CONTROL  properties: { label: "L-${record.id}" }
         -> DOM shows "L-rec_1"                              RESOLVES  (record scope is live, instrument fires)

CASE A   node-level params: { recordId: "${record.id}" }
         -> handler received {"recordId":"${record.id}"}     RAW

CASE B   properties: { params: { recordId: "${record.id}" } }
         -> handler received {"recordId":"${record.id}"}     RAW
```

Case B is the interesting one. `properties` **is** an evaluating channel — that is objectui#7849's whole point — but `SchemaRenderer`'s memo evaluates it **per value and shallowly** (`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`, "Per-value and SHALLOW, matching the `props` branch exactly"). A `params` object under `properties` is one value; the template sitting one level inside it is never visited. ⚠️ So objectui#7849's "`properties` works" holds only at depth 1, and that qualification is worth carrying there.

## Why no other channel closes it

- **The row is not injected.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/DeclaredActionsBar.tsx:110` says it in as many words: *"injects the record under `params._rowRecord` — which `action:button` does NOT do, and which the api handler needs to resolve `{id}` and inject the record id."*
- **The resolver has no context fallback for `recordId`, deliberately.** `packages/app-shell/src/utils/recordFormNavigation.ts:286-287`: *"`recordId` is read from `action.params.recordId` or `action.recordId` (no context fallback — record ids are intrinsically per-action)."* `objectName` has a three-step ladder ending in `context.objectName`; `recordId` has none.
- **`action.recordId` is not forwarded.** `action-button.tsx:150-219` forwards an explicit whitelist, and neither `recordId` nor `objectName` is on it. `params` is the only door.

⇒ the three doors are all shut: no template, no row injection, no context fallback.

## Consequence, and what objectui#7440's PR had to do about it

`content/docs/guide/record-edit-modes.md` taught `"recordId": "${record.id}"` inside that bag. Repairing only the action-name key would have published a second silently-inert example — the button would reach the handler and navigate to `/apps/sales/account/record/%24%7Brecord.id%7D/edit`. PR #7865 therefore publishes a literal id plus a note, and points per-row Edit at the built-in entry point. That is an honest doc, not a fix for this gap.

## The fork (⛔ not proposing a disposition)

- **Evaluate `params` values** (deep, or one documented level) in the same memo that already evaluates `properties`. Widest blast radius: every action on every surface.
- **Let `action:button` stash the row** the way `DeclaredActionsBar` does. That file's comment reads as a deliberate difference, so it needs a ruling, not a patch.
- **Give `resolveNavigateEditUrl` a context `recordId` leg.** Narrowest, and squarely against the reason its docblock states.
- **Rule it out of scope** — page-mode edit is reached from the built-in Edit affordance, and a declared `navigate_edit` is only ever for a known record. Then the doc note added by PR #7865 is the whole answer and this card closes as documented-by-design.

All four are accept-set or behaviour changes on published packages. ⛔ Nothing was changed for this finding.

## Dedup

Scanned the 191 open issues carrying `finding` or `documentation` (repo-scoped REST listings, paged to exhaustion; the control terms `navigate_create` / `navigate_edit` / `action:button` returned objectui#7440 and only it, so the instrument fires).

Nearest siblings, both read and both distinct:

- **objectui#7849** — `properties` evaluates and hoists templates but the unevaluated-expression diagnostic omits it. Same channel, different question: it is about the **diagnostic's** channel list; this is about the channel's **depth** and about a bag no channel reaches. The depth datum above belongs on it.
- **objectui#7680** — `schema-rendering.md` teaches a chart binding node-level `data` to a template that is not evaluated. Same family (`${…}` in a non-evaluating position), different key, different page, and it is a parse refusal on top; this one is not refused by anything.
